DOC-31-P50-PART2-Q51.exam_ready_answer:
• Method: Use an operator stack based on operator precedence: () > ^ > *, / > +, -.
• Table of Execution: [Symbol Scanned, Stack Contents, Output Expression].
• Operands pass directly to output; operators wait on stack until lower precedence arrives.
• Final Postfix Expression is verified parenthesis-free.
DOC-31-P50-PART2-Q51.common_mistakes: Treating ^ as left-associative instead of right-associative, or outputting '(' into the postfix string.
DOC-31-P50-PART2-Q51.beginner_notes: Operands never touch the stack; only operators and parentheses enter the stack.

DOC-31-P59-PART2-Q59.time_complexity: Divide-and-conquer partitioning (Complexity derivation excluded per syllabus)
DOC-31-P59-PART2-Q59.space_complexity: O(log n) to O(n) call stack space
DOC-31-P59-PART2-Q59.direct_answer: Partitions array around a pivot such that left elements ≤ pivot ≤ right elements.
DOC-31-P59-PART2-Q59.step_by_step_explanation:
1. Select a pivot element (e.g. last element A[high] in Lomuto scheme).
2. Maintain partition index i starting at low - 1.
3. Scan j from low to high - 1: if A[j] ≤ pivot, advance i++ and swap A[i] with A[j].
4. Swap A[i + 1] with A[high] to place pivot in its permanent sorted location pi = i + 1.
5. Recursively invoke QuickSort on left subarray A[low .. pi - 1] and right subarray A[pi + 1 .. high].
6. NOTE: Complexity analysis derivation is explicitly excluded by the locked syllabus.
DOC-31-P59-PART2-Q59.exam_ready_answer:
• Core Principle: Divide-and-conquer partitioning.
• Partition Procedure: Rearranges array so elements < pivot are left, elements > pivot are right.
• Pivot is permanently placed in its correct sorted position.
• Recursive calls sort the left and right partitions independently.
DOC-31-P59-PART2-Q59.common_mistakes: Attempting full recurrence relations or worst-case derivations (which are excluded from syllabus!).

• Deleting node X without head pointer: Copy data of X->next to X, bypass X->next.

3. Row-Major Address Formula: Addr(A[i][j]) = Base + w · [ (i - L1) · C + (j - L2) ].
4. Column-Major Address Formula: Addr(A[i][j]) = Base + w · [ (j - L2) · R + (i - L1) ].

DOC-31-P82-PART2-Q86.space_complexity: O(1) iterative, O(log n) recursive call stack
DOC-31-P82-PART2-Q86.direct_answer: Divides sorted search interval in half by comparing key with middle element.
DOC-31-P82-PART2-Q86.step_by_step_explanation:
1. Precondition: Array MUST be sorted.
2. Initialize low = 0, high = n - 1.
3. While low ≤ high:
   - Calculate mid = low + (high - low) / 2 (avoids integer overflow).
   - If arr[mid] == key: return mid (Found).
   - If arr[mid] < key: search right half, set low = mid + 1.
   - If arr[mid] > key: search left half, set high = mid - 1.
4. If low > high: return -1 (Not found).
5. Worst Case Recurrence: T(n) = T(n/2) + 1. Solution: T(n) = ⌊log2 n⌋ + 1 = O(log n).
DOC-31-P82-PART2-Q86.exam_ready_answer:
• Precondition: Input array must be strictly sorted.
• Recurrence Relation: T(n) = T(n/2) + c.
• Worst Case Time Complexity: ⌊log2 n⌋ + 1 = O(log n).
• Mid calculation formula: mid = low + (high - low) / 2.
DOC-31-P82-PART2-Q86.common_mistakes: Applying binary search on unsorted arrays, or using (low + high) / 2 without overflow guard.
DOC-31-P82-PART2-Q86.beginner_notes: Each comparison cuts the search space in half. 1,000,000 items takes at most 20 comparisons.

DOC-31-P83-PART2-Q89.direct_answer: Pointer manipulation updating next links in-place.
DOC-31-P83-PART2-Q89.step_by_step_explanation:
1. Node definition: struct Node { int data; struct Node* next; };
2. For Reversal: Use three pointers: prev = NULL, curr = head, next = NULL.
3. Loop while curr != NULL: save next = curr->next; reverse link curr->next = prev; advance prev = curr; curr = next.
4. Update head = prev.
5. For Deletion of node X without head: Copy data from X->next into X, then delete X->next (X->next = X->next->next). Valid if X is not the last node.
DOC-31-P83-PART2-Q89.exam_ready_answer:
• Reversal requires 3 pointers: prev (NULL), curr (head), next (NULL).
• In-place update: `next = curr->next; curr->next = prev; prev = curr; curr = next;`
• Time Complexity: O(n), Space Complexity: O(1).
• Deleting node X without head pointer: Copy data of X->next to X, bypass X->next.
DOC-31-P83-PART2-Q89.common_mistakes: Losing the next node pointer before redirecting curr->next.
DOC-31-P83-PART2-Q89.beginner_notes: Always store `curr->next` in a temporary pointer before breaking the link.

DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.time_complexity: Divide-and-conquer partitioning (Complexity derivation excluded per syllabus)
DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.space_complexity: O(log n) to O(n) call stack space
DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.direct_answer: Partitions array around a pivot such that left elements ≤ pivot ≤ right elements.
DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.step_by_step_explanation:
1. Select a pivot element (e.g. last element A[high] in Lomuto scheme).
2. Maintain partition index i starting at low - 1.
3. Scan j from low to high - 1: if A[j] ≤ pivot, advance i++ and swap A[i] with A[j].
4. Swap A[i + 1] with A[high] to place pivot in its permanent sorted location pi = i + 1.
5. Recursively invoke QuickSort on left subarray A[low .. pi - 1] and right subarray A[pi + 1 .. high].
6. NOTE: Complexity analysis derivation is explicitly excluded by the locked syllabus.
DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.exam_ready_answer:
• Core Principle: Divide-and-conquer partitioning.
• Partition Procedure: Rearranges array so elements < pivot are left, elements > pivot are right.
• Pivot is permanently placed in its correct sorted position.
• Recursive calls sort the left and right partitions independently.
DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.common_mistakes: Attempting full recurrence relations or worst-case derivations (which are excluded from syllabus!).
DOC-31-P186-PART2-Q177.beginner_notes: Once partitioned, the pivot never moves again.
